studies.label: Main five-condition, two-round plastic-pollution ideation experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1; qualified by PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.6 and 4.1
counts_source.quote: A total of 254 adult participants were initially enrolled, and seven were removed for failing attention checks or offering cursory responses, resulting in a final sample size of 247.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: No external suggestions in either ideation round. Source: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4.

arms.name: Early-AI-Labeled
arms.description: Pre-generated GPT-4 suggestions supplied in the initial ideation round under the heading AI-generated ideas, with bold text and an icon. No new external inputs in the final round; continued access to the earlier suggestions is not stated. Source: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4.

arms.name: Early-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: The same early GPT-4 suggestions supplied under the heading Ideas from others, without AI attribution. No new external inputs in the final round; continued access to the earlier suggestions is not stated. Source: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4.

arms.name: Late-AI-Labeled
arms.description: Initial ideation without suggestions; the same GPT-4 suggestions supplied at the start of the final round under the heading AI-generated ideas, with bold text and an icon. Source: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4.

arms.name: Late-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: Initial ideation without suggestions; the same GPT-4 suggestions supplied at the start of the final round under the heading Ideas from others, without AI attribution. Source: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4.

studies.task: Propose innovative, feasible solutions to urban plastic pollution, then refine, expand, combine, or replace those solutions in a second ideation round.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3; specific model version and release year not stated

estimates.outcome: Expert-rated overall creativity of the final submission
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Modified Consensual Assessment Technique. Three domain experts in environmental policy or innovation management independently rated final ideas on seven-point novelty, usefulness, and originality scales. The overall-creativity formula and aggregation across experts or ideas are not specified. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5.

sources.quote: and the Control yielding the lowest (M = 4.94).
Late-AI groups, conversely, reported a more pronounced “pivot,” generating more diver- gent ideas than Early-AI but still exceeding the Control in final outcomes.
Three do- main experts with backgrounds in environmental policy or in- novation management independently assessed each final idea on novelty, usefulness, and originality, using 7-point scales.
Late-AI participants now received the same GPT-4 sug- gestions, again labeled or unlabeled according to condition. Early-AI and Control participants proceeded without new ex- ternal inputs.

estimates.notes: Section 4.1 says the Late-AI groups exceeded Control in final outcomes. This arm-specific record retains that reported ordering and the printed Control mean; it does not reconstruct a pooled Late-AI estimate. The treatment mean, both arm SDs, and numerical pairwise test, effect, and uncertainty are not printed. Figure 2a displays arm levels and error bars without numerical labels; no values or p-value thresholds are inferred from the graph. The omnibus condition ANOVA and its partial eta-squared do not test this two-arm contrast. Exact analyzed people counts are unresolved after screening. Each participant contributes a final submission, but the score aggregation is incompletely described. The outcome was produced with suggestions supplied during the final round; this is a between-arm comparison, not a randomized-order within-person design.

estimates.outcome: Semantic distance of the final submission from GPT-4 suggestions
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Participant submissions were embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 and compared with each GPT-4 suggestion using cosine similarity; results are called semantic distance, with lower distance indicating more overlap. The similarity-to-distance transformation and aggregation across suggestions are not specified. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Figure 2 caption and panel a
sources.quote: Figure 2: Results showing (a) creativity scores and semantic distances across conditions, (b) comparison of AI influence between labeled and unlabeled conditions,
Late-AI participants now received the same GPT-4 sug- gestions, again labeled or unlabeled according to condition. Early-AI and Control participants proceeded without new ex- ternal inputs.

estimates.notes: Figure 2a contains a bracket marked **** between the light-blue Late-AI-Labeled and purple Late-AI-Unlabeled semantic-distance bars; the shared legend identifies the arms. This contrast is shown graphically, with no numerical arm levels, SDs, pairwise statistic, or defined p-value threshold. No number is read from bar heights, error bars, or asterisks. Labeled suggestions are the tested transparency configuration and unlabeled suggestions are the reference. Higher distance means less overlap with the supplied AI suggestions, not greater diversity across different people; higher_is is therefore other. The means and test in Section 4.2 combine early and late timing conditions and cannot be substituted for this late-only contrast. There is no numerical pairwise uncertainty to classify; se_basis is not_reported. Exact participant counts and the number of underlying text pairs are not reported for this analysis.

estimates.outcome: Change in expert-rated overall creativity from Round 1 to Round 2
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Modified Consensual Assessment Technique. Three domain experts in environmental policy or innovation management independently rated final ideas on seven-point novelty, usefulness, and originality scales. The overall-creativity formula and aggregation across experts or ideas are not specified. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5.

stats.difference_is: treatment minus control in change from Round 1 to Round 2

sources.quote: Meanwhile, the Control group changed min- imally across rounds (+0.14),

To assess these within-participant changes more rigorously, we used a repeated-measures ANOVA on creativity scores from Round 1 and Round 2, confirming that Late-AI conditions drove significantly larger improve- ments over time than their Early-AI or Control counterparts.
Three do- main experts with backgrounds in environmental policy or in- novation management independently assessed each final idea on novelty, usefulness, and originality, using 7-point scales.
Late-AI participants now received the same GPT-4 sug- gestions, again labeled or unlabeled according to condition. Early-AI and Control participants proceeded without new ex- ternal inputs.

estimates.notes: Section 4.4 reports that the Late-AI conditions improved more than Control in a repeated-measures analysis. Separate records retain the two randomized Late-AI arms without assuming an unreported pooled-arm estimate. control_mean is the printed mean change, not the final score. The Late-AI increase is described only as a maximum, without identifying which labeling arm or aggregation it describes, so treatment_mean is null. The printed Late-AI within-group change test and standardized effect are not a test or effect for the randomized difference in change and are not entered here. No between-arm change coefficient, numerical test, SE, or CI is supplied. within_person is null because this record compares randomized arms; condition order was not randomized. Both rounds occurred in the same session. The methods describe expert scoring of final submissions but do not separately specify scoring of the initial round. Figure 2e contains unlabeled trajectories; its largest creativity gain appears under the Early-AI-Labeled legend entry, in conflict with the prose attribution to Late-AI. No graph values or alternative arm attribution are inferred. Exact analysis counts remain null.

not_extracted.what: S2: Preparatory pilot for GPT-4 suggestion selection and editing
not_extracted.reason: Stimulus evaluation and editing; no randomized AI-assisted human production task or eligible human-output contrast is described. The reported pilot n is not explicitly identified as people. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3: "Prior to finalizing these AI prompts, we conducted a small pilot study (n = 15) to verify that the suggestions were con- sistent in length, clarity, and perceived originality."

not_extracted.what: S1: Baseline Alternative Uses Task fluency
not_extracted.reason: Measured before the ideation manipulation and used as a baseline predictor, not an outcome of randomized AI assistance. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4.

not_extracted.what: S1: Trust in AI
not_extracted.reason: Baseline self-report and moderator, not a score on a produced creative output. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.3.

not_extracted.what: S1: Perceived external influence, labeled versus unlabeled suggestions
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported influence of the suggestions, not creativity scored on participants' produced work. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2 and Figure 2b.

not_extracted.what: S1: Creative self-efficacy
not_extracted.reason: Post-task self-report, not a score on the produced output. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.4 and 3.5.

not_extracted.what: S1: Source recognition of unlabeled suggestions
not_extracted.reason: Recognition of the origin of supplied AI work, not creativity scored on human-produced output. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2.

not_extracted.what: S1: Response or processing time
not_extracted.reason: Platform process measure, not a creativity or diversity score on produced work; no eligible outcome contrast is reported. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Figure 1.

not_extracted.what: S1: Qualitative interviews on awareness, ownership, authenticity, and labeling
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported experiences in a selected subset of the main sample; no independent randomized study or scored-output treatment contrast. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.2; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 10285), Section 4.5.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Final creativity for Early-AI-Labeled versus Control, Early-AI-Unlabeled versus Control, and timing comparisons involving Early-AI arms
not_extracted.reason: Continued access to earlier AI suggestions during final production is not established, so neither with_ai nor after_ai can be confirmed for Early-AI final outcomes. This also affects the early-versus-late pairwise brackets in Figure 2a. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4: "Early-AI and Control participants proceeded without new ex- ternal inputs." The printed Early-AI-Labeled descriptive result is preserved as context only: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1: "with Early-AI-Labeled achieving the highest mean (M = 6.01, SD = 0.48) and the Control yielding the lowest (M = 4.94)."

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Change in creativity for Early-AI arms versus Control and Late-AI versus Early-AI arms
not_extracted.reason: The Early-AI final-round availability uncertainty prevents assigning these change contrasts to a confirmed question. This is not evidence of an after_ai outcome. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.4.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Expert-rated novelty of the final submission
not_extracted.reason: Only an omnibus condition ANOVA is reported. No specific eligible two-arm contrast or arm descriptives are supplied, and the omnibus result is not assigned to an AI-versus-Control comparison. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Expert-rated usefulness of the final submission
not_extracted.reason: Only an omnibus condition ANOVA is reported. No specific eligible two-arm contrast or arm descriptives are supplied, and the omnibus result is not assigned to an AI-versus-Control comparison. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: Expert-rated originality of the final submission
not_extracted.reason: Originality is rated separately from novelty, but only an omnibus condition ANOVA is reported. There is no reported two-arm contrast or arm descriptive result; a nonsignificant omnibus result is not a zero treatment effect. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.5 and 4.1.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Omnibus final-creativity condition ANOVA and partial eta-squared
not_extracted.reason: The test involves all conditions and is not an effect or uncertainty estimate for a specified two-arm contrast. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1: "F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial η2 = .38."

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Early-AI-Labeled versus Control and early-versus-late final semantic-distance comparisons
not_extracted.reason: These comparisons include Early-AI final submissions, for which suggestion availability is unresolved. They cannot be confirmed as with_ai or after_ai. The measure compares submissions with AI exemplars and is not across_people diversity. The late-labeled versus late-unlabeled graphical comparison is retained separately. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.4, 3.5 and 4.1; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Figure 2a.

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Early-AI-Labeled and Late-AI-Labeled (combined) versus Early-AI-Unlabeled and Late-AI-Unlabeled (combined)
not_extracted.reason: The pooled labeling contrast includes Early-AI final outcomes whose with_ai versus after_ai status is unresolved. It cannot be reassigned to the late-only comparison or treated as across-person diversity. The printed positive d is retained here exactly despite the negative t and lower labeled mean: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2: "Labeled participants also exhibited closer textual overlap with the AI (semantic distance of .61 vs. .73, t = −11.04, p < .001, d = 1.58)."

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Omnibus final semantic-distance condition ANOVA and eta-squared
not_extracted.reason: Omnibus condition effect, not a specific two-arm contrast. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Late-AI within-group creativity increase from the first round to the final round
not_extracted.reason: A before-after change within Late-AI participants, not a randomized-order paired contrast or a between-arm treatment effect. The particular Late-AI arm or aggregation is not identified. Its test and effect size cannot supply precision for the retained between-arm change comparisons. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.4: "Comparisons of Rounds (Figure 2e) showed Late-AI par- ticipants demonstrating the largest boosts in creativity (in- creases up to +0.88; t = −19.69, p < .001, d = 1.73)"

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Late-AI within-group change in semantic distance
not_extracted.reason: Before-after change following AI introduction, without randomized condition order or a reported between-arm change contrast. The particular labeling arm or aggregation is not identified. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.4.

not_extracted.what: S1: Baseline-creativity-by-condition and trust moderation, including Table 1 simple slopes
not_extracted.reason: Moderator analyses, not full-sample AI treatment effects. The table slopes and SEs describe the association of baseline fluency with final creativity within conditions. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.3, Table 1 and Figure 2d.

not_extracted.what: S1: Correlation of perceived external influence with semantic distance
not_extracted.reason: Association with a post-treatment self-report, not a randomized contrast on an output score. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2 and Figure 2c.

not_extracted.what: S1: Initial-round creativity and semantic-distance trajectories in Figure 2e
not_extracted.reason: Initial-round levels are shown only graphically, with no identified first-round two-arm test or printed descriptive statistics. The paper does not report a randomized-order crossover design. No new pairwise contrast or numeric level is constructed from the trajectories. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Figure 2e and Section 4.4.

open_items: Original numbers randomized overall and by arm, exclusion timing, and the final analysis denominators are not confirmed. Section 3.1 reports enrollment, specified exclusions, and arm counts, but Section 3.6 adds outlier and incomplete-response screening without counts; the reported omnibus degrees of freedom are inconsistent with the stated final headcount. No counts are inferred from degrees of freedom.
Recruitment frame, occupational or student composition, country, and physical administration setting are not stated. A web interface alone does not establish an online panel or remote setting.
Continued visibility of Early-AI suggestions during final production is unknown. Clarification is needed to assign early final-output and pooled labeling contrasts to with_ai or after_ai.

No numerical late-arm final creativity means, arm SDs, pairwise effects, SEs, confidence limits, or pairwise test statistics are printed. The Control final mean alone cannot establish the magnitude or precision of either contrast.
Figure 2a gives no numerical late-arm semantic-distance means or uncertainty and does not define the p-value thresholds represented by its asterisks.
Overall-creativity scoring and aggregation across experts and multiple ideas are not specified; the initial-round expert-rating procedure is also not separately described.
The cosine-similarity-to-distance transformation and aggregation across AI suggestions are not provided. The number of underlying text pairs is not reported.

The Late-AI arm or aggregation behind the reported maximum creativity increase and within-group tests is not identified. No between-arm change coefficient or numerical uncertainty is printed. Section 4.4 and the Figure 2e legend/trajectories disagree about which group has the largest creativity gain.
GPT-4 is named, but its specific version and release year are not given in the paper.

The pilot count does not clearly identify its units, and pilot overlap with the main sample is not stated. No separate appendix, supplement, data repository, or code repository is named that resolves these omissions.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-11. Read the complete markdown conversion in order, including all references; extracted and checked all PDF pages with PyMuPDF. There is no appendix in this document. Figure 2 was inspected from an in-memory PDF rendering; no graph numbers were estimated. Only the main randomized experiment is included in studies; the stimulus pilot is listed in not_extracted, and the interviews are a subset of the main experiment. No external sample reuse is stated. The screening form is used as a map. Its online_rct designation rests on web-platform delivery, but the paper does not establish an online panel, remote participation, supervised laboratory, or ordinary-work setting; the current codebook permits unstated_rct, used here. Population remains null and country is empty because adult convenience sampling does not identify a population category. The reported arm allocation passage is PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1: "These participants were randomly assigned to five conditions: Control (n = 50), Early-AI Labeled (n = 49), Early-AI Un- labeled (n = 49), Late-AI Labeled (n = 50), and Late-AI Unlabeled (n = 49)." These counts and the reported final sample in counts_source are not treated as confirmed analysis denominators because further screening is unquantified. The initially enrolled count is not equated with randomized people. All structured person counts remain null. Early-AI final-output availability remains unresolved as in the reconciled screening decision; those contrasts, including the pooled labeling comparison, are documented in not_extracted instead of assigning an unsupported question. Late-AI final outputs have confirmed AI assistance. The final creativity and change comparisons are stated for Late-AI conditions in the plural; separate arm records preserve that wording without asserting that the paper estimated a pooled Late-AI contrast. The additional late-only semantic-distance contrast is explicitly bracketed in Figure 2a although not listed separately in the screening map. The retained comparisons have no numerical between-arm uncertainty. Omnibus tests, moderator slopes, within-group change effects, and pooled labeling statistics are not reused as pairwise effects. Means, SDs, differences, effects, or people counts have not been calculated. Numeric sources use PDF text with whitespace normalized only; line-break hyphens are preserved. No preregistration or primary outcome is stated.
